newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DEC Hungary unit eyes HUF 10 bln '97 sales.
newsitem.headline: DEC Hungary unit eyes HUF 10 bln '97 sales.

text.p: The Hungarian unit of Digital Equipment Corp has targeted sales of 10 billion forints this year, compared with some seven billion in 1996, company officials said on Tuesday.
"Our sales target is some 10 billion forints for 1997," Gyorgy Beck, Digital Hungary's general director, told a news conference.

He added that in 1996 the company had some seven billion forints of sales compared with five billion in 1995. He also said that these figures are approximate as DEC's business year runs from July 1 to June 30.
Last year's record turnover was due to a very strong fourth quarter, Beck said.

"The (Hungarian) market saw a boom at the end of last year and we managed to take advantage of it," he said, adding that Results also benefited from a breakthrough of the 64-bit technology pioneered by Digital.
"In 1995 we were almost alone in preaching the advantages of 64-bit technology," Beck said. "In 1996 most others joined the bandwagon".
Consequently, Hungarian sales of Digital's flagship TurboLaser server have doubled to some 100 units last year, he said.
Another company official said the Alpha microprocessor has further room for growth.
"We will shortly reach the 600 megahertz clock speed and the pace of the rise will remain unbroken even after that," said Laszlo Mezriczky.
PC sales have also grown considerably last year, with sales of portable computers rising the fastest.
"In 1994 we sold 90 portable machines and last year almost 1,000," said Attila Nemeth, head of Digital Hungary's PC division.

However, the company was not so successful in promoting its Microsoft support centre, Internet-related products and taking advantage of Hungarian companies outsourcing their information technology needs, Beck said.
"Outsourcing simply did not happen at the pace we expected it to," he said.
He also said that Digital's share of Hungary's $500 million to $600 million a year information technology market was "slightly below ten percent".
Beck added that they will shortly announce the creation of a leasing company, in partnership with one of the major domestic leasing firms, to finance sales.
